title: Revivals of Bell nonlocality require Schrödinger and Heisenberg non-Markovianity
summary: Bell nonlocality is a key resource in quantum information, demonstrating the nonclassicality of quantum theory. Noise, however, is in general detrimental to nonlocality, and can cause the loss of the ability to violate any Bell inequality. Memory effects, on the other hand, can restore this quantumness and, as recently shown, they can be differently characterized in the Schrödinger and in the Heisenberg picture.
